what: Host Hotels is the largest publicly traded hotel property owner in the United States. It owns 76 luxury and upper-upscale hotels but does not run them: Marriott, Hyatt and others operate them under management agreements.
customers: Business, group and leisure travellers staying at its hotels, through the brands that manage them.
money: rooms, food and beverage and other hotel income
moat: Large convention and resort hotels in locations that cannot be replicated, where building a comparable property today would cost far more than their carrying value.
risks: Hotel demand falls sharply in a recession
Group and business travel has recovered unevenly
opportunities: Revenue grew about 8% last year and about 8% a year over three years
A dividend yield around 3% with a strong balance sheet for the sector
Very little new luxury hotel supply is being built in its markets
watch: Revenue per available room and group booking pace.
